claims.text: The initial HEA has a roughly homogeneous distribution of constituent elements.
High configurational entropy drives selective segregation of reactive elements in HEAs.
Reactive elements such as Cr or Al preferentially segregate toward grain boundaries and the surface at high temperatures.
At high temperatures, reactive elements diffuse through the HEA toward grain boundaries and the surface.
Localized enrichment of reactive elements facilitates nucleation and growth of a uniform oxide layer.
Localized enrichment of reactive elements promotes formation of an adherent oxide layer.
The protective oxide is expected to consist of an oxide such as Cr2O3 or Al2O3.
A continuous oxide layer limits further oxygen ingress.
Limiting oxygen ingress enhances oxidation resistance.
Relative to conventional alloys or nonsegregating HEAs, the test HEA will form a more uniform oxide film.
Relative to conventional alloys or nonsegregating HEAs, the test HEA will form a more adherent oxide film.
The test HEA will exhibit a reduced oxide-scale growth rate relative to the baseline.
The test HEA will sustain less overall oxidation damage over time than the baseline.
Conventional alloys or HEAs without significant segregation typically form less uniform or poorly adherent oxide layers.
Conventional alloys or HEAs without significant segregation typically exhibit faster scale growth and higher oxidation rates.
The proposed mechanism applies at temperatures where diffusion kinetics are active.
The proposed mechanism requires sufficient concentrations of reactive elements.
The proposed mechanism may not apply at lower temperatures or in HEAs whose compositions do not facilitate segregation.
Increasing Cr or Al content is expected to produce a more uniform and adherent oxide layer with improved oxidation resistance.
Increasing Cr or Al content is expected to produce a thicker oxide layer.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome emphasizes a reduced oxide-scale growth rate, whereas the falsification rule treats formation of a thicker oxide layer as an expected favorable result. Without specifying time-dependent kinetics or a target thickness, these expectations conflict.
